newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S./Canadian group plans Chile natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: U.S./Canadian group plans Chile natgas pipeline.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp said it has reached an agreement with Canada's NOVA Corp to build a natural gas pipeline from northern Argentina to Chile and a gas-fired power plant which will involve an investment of $700 million.

"NOVA will contribute its experience of markets, permits and contruction which it acquired with the GasAndes pipeline," said William Harner, president of CMS Gas Transmission and Storage, in a statement released in Santiago.
NOVA is one of the partners in the GasAndes pipeline project which is being built to supply Santiago with natural gas from Mendoza in central Argentina.
The second pipeline, known as Gasoducto Atacama, will cross the Andes and the Atacama Desert from Salta in northern Argentina to the Chilean port of Mejillones.
CMS and NOVA plan to build a 400 megawatt gas-fired power plant to power the region's fast growing mining industry.
"We hope that gas-fired electricity generation will compete advantageously with existing coal plants in the north of Chile," said Francisco Mezzadri, CMS's regional representative for Latin America.
Construction of the project will begin in mid-1997 with the plant coming on stream in early 1999, said the statement.
Power demand in the region, the heart of Chile's copper mining industry, will rise steeply in coming years as existing mines expand and new pits come into production.
